name: coding_read
description: Use when a comfort or lighting function behaves oddly or is missing (daytime lights, coming-home, needle sweep) and module coding may explain it.
instructions: Call read_coding {} once: it reads each codeable module's long coding and lists up to 12 decoded fields per module.
The first line per module is "<module>: coding <hex>"; each field line is "- <name>: <value>", a single bit reading on or off.
This phase reads only; to change a value the owner uses the Adaptations / Coding screens. Never tell the owner the agent changed or will change a coding.
Fields marked unconfirmed come from bit positions not yet checked on this car: quote them as indicative and say so.
interpret: Coding bit positions are manufacturer- and module-specific and come from this car's profile and label packs; the hex is exactly what the module returned.
A function the owner misses whose bit reads off is a likely explanation; a bit that reads on while the function does not work points at wiring, a bulb or the module, not at coding.
"no answer" means the module did not return its coding (asleep, not fitted or another address): it is not a fault.
Coding never explains engine, emission or warning-light faults on its own: use it only for comfort, lighting and convenience functions, and never base an urgent verdict on an unconfirmed field.
